newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi and private firms to build aromatics complex.
newsitem.headline: Saudi and private firms to build aromatics complex.

text.p: Saudi and international firms intend to invest 225 million Saudi riyals ($60 million) in a world-scale petrochemical plant in the Saudi industrial city of Yanbu, the project's backers said in a statement on Monday.

Saudi Arabian firm Universal Petrochemical Co Ltd has teamed up with Germany's Phenolchemie GmbH and the U.K.'s Saudi-British Economic Offset Office, to build the export-orientated plant in the Red Sea city.

"This project consititutes a part of the Saudi-British Defence Agreement (Al-Yamamah)," the statement said. "Its objectives are to support and enourage the transfer of technology and technical know-how to Saudi companies through mutual projects."
The Saudi-British Offset Office was set up as part of the $2 billion Al-Yamamah oil-for-arms deal to administer investment in the Kingdom.
The 260,000 tonnes a year capacity plant will specialise in producing cumene and is expected to be operational in 1998.
Cumene is used to produce phenol and acetone for the manufacture of products such as building materials, carpets, automotive parts, cosmetics and medicines.

"Phenolchemie...shall off-lift the highest ratio of the product in order to satisfy its requirements while the rest of the product will be exported to India and Asian Pacific countries," the statement said.
The project will receive industrial loans and custom exemptions from the Saudi government covering the import of equipment needed for the production of cumene.
Contacts had been made with state-oil firm Saudi Aramco and petrochemical giant SABIC to secure necessary feedstock.

Saudi Arabia has highlighted the domestic petrochemical industry and private investment in that sector as the cornerstone of its industrialisation drive and central to its drive to diversify its oil-dominated economy.
